+## Metrics
+
+`kvstore_get_value_requests_total{outcome}` (api.py) counts every
+`get_value` call, labeled `success` or `error`. It's enough to alert on a
+spike in the `error` label; it says nothing about staleness, unbounded
+cache growth, or storage collisions, since a cache hit looks the same
+whether or not the value is correct.

Phase 2 -- failure modes: document every way this service can fail as FailureMode
entries, each with a stable ID, a severity (`critical` demands immediate human
intervention and pages; `warning` demands action soon and files a ticket), a
`user_visible` flag, and -- for a user-visible failure -- its upstream causes named by

First principles for this analysis (spec, "What Blare is"):

- Alerting is the target. Documenting failure modes is the first step, not the goal;
  every failure mode must end in an alert recommendation or an explicit, reasoned
  exclusion.
- Failure chains, not just user-visible ends. A user-visible failure is usually the
  last link of a chain. Document the upstream links as failure modes in their own
  right so each can be detected as early as possible.

Let me ground this fully in the code before drafting entries — I've already read `api.py`, `cache.py`, `storage.py`, `evictor.py`, and `admin.py`, and want to check one more subtlety (encoding-related exceptions bypassing `StorageError`) before finalizing the chain structure.

Confirmed: `storage.py` only catches `OSError`, using the platform-default text codec with no explicit `encoding=`. A `UnicodeDecodeError`/`UnicodeEncodeError` (e.g. a value with characters outside that codec's range, or a file corrupted with non-decodable bytes) would propagate uncaught — bypassing `StorageError` entirely, and therefore bypassing `api.py`'s `except StorageError` too. That's a distinct, non-obvious failure mode worth its own chain link.

Here's the full model I'm proposing — 7 root-cause entries (not directly user-visible, each a place to detect earlier) feeding 5 user-visible symptom entries, plus removing my earlier one-off entry that these supersede with proper chains:

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get() fails to read the backing flat file
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get() (storage.py) wraps any OSError raised while checking for/reading the backing file (permission denied, disk I/O error, path unreadable) as StorageError. Occurs on every get_value call that misses the cache while the file is in this state.
payload_or_id.impact: Every cache-missing get_value call for any key fails until the underlying condition (permissions, disk) is fixed.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() fails to persist a write
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (storage.py) wraps any OSError raised while reading the existing file, creating parent directories, or writing the replacement file as StorageError. Reachable only via admin.update_value(), the internal write path used by an external periodic data-sync job -- not directly by get_value.
payload_or_id.impact: The intended new value never reaches storage; nothing in this codebase surfaces the failure (admin.update_value has no try/except of its own), so it is only as visible as whatever the external caller does with a raised exception.

payload_or_id.title: admin.update_value writes to storage without invalidating the cache
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() (admin.py) calls storage.put(key, value) but never calls Cache.evict(key). Any reader who has already cached that key -- including a cached negative ('not found') result from before the key existed -- keeps observing the pre-write value or absence indefinitely, since nothing else in the read path re-validates a cached entry against storage.
payload_or_id.impact: Establishes the divergence between cache and storage that later manifests to a client as a stale read.

payload_or_id.title: evictor.run_eviction_pass never evicts any entry (seconds vs. milliseconds bug)
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (evictor.py) computes now = time.time() (seconds) and compares now - entry.inserted_at_ms (milliseconds) against TTL_SECONDS. Because inserted_at_ms is ~1000x larger than a seconds-based now, the difference is always a large negative number and the 'expired' condition is never true. No entry is ever evicted, for any key, ever.
payload_or_id.impact: Removes the only safety net that would otherwise bound both cache size and how long a stale entry can persist -- it is the root cause of both unbounded memory growth and permanent (rather than TTL-bounded) staleness.

payload_or_id.title: Storage's flat-file format has no escaping for its comma/newline delimiters
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/put (storage.py) persist one 'key,value' pair per line using an unescaped comma and split records on newlines via splitlines(). A key containing a comma is truncated to the text before its first comma on read (str.partition(',')), so it can silently match a different, shorter key's line. A value containing a newline is re-split into extra spurious lines on the next read, corrupting how subsequent lines in the file are parsed.
payload_or_id.impact: Root cause of a client silently receiving another key's value, or of downstream file entries becoming unparseable, with no exception raised anywhere.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no locking
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (storage.py) reads the whole file into an `existing` dict, updates one key, then rewrites the whole file. Two put() calls whose read/write windows interleave each build `existing` from a stale snapshot; whichever writes last overwrites the other's change with no error raised to either caller.
payload_or_id.impact: A legitimate write can be silently dropped under concurrent writers, with the same client-visible effect as a stale read for the lost key. Requires more than one concurrent writer of the internal write path to manifest.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get/put only catch OSError, not the full space of I/O-adjacent exceptions
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/put (storage.py) call Path.read_text()/write_text() with no explicit encoding, using the platform's default text codec, and catch only 'except OSError'. A value containing characters not encodable in that codec raises UnicodeEncodeError from put(); a file containing bytes not decodable in that codec (including as a side effect of fm-storage-flatfile-delimiter-ambiguity corrupting the file) raises UnicodeDecodeError from get(). Neither is an OSError, so neither is wrapped as StorageError.
payload_or_id.impact: The exception reaches api.get_value() as a type its 'except StorageError' clause does not match, so it is not merely undetected by the outcome metric -- it skips that except block entirely and the metric is not incremented at all, breaking get_value's implicit contract that failures surface as StorageError.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) raises StorageError to its caller
payload_or_id.description: api.get_value() (api.py) catches StorageError only to record GET_VALUE_REQUESTS{outcome="error"} before re-raising it unchanged. A client's call throws instead of returning a value.
payload_or_id.impact: The sole client-facing operation fails outright for the affected key(s) until the underlying storage condition clears.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) returns successfully with a stale value
payload_or_id.description: A client's get_value call returns without error but with a value (or a cached 'not found') that no longer matches current storage, because Cache.get() serves whatever it captured on first read/miss with nothing in the read path re-validating it. Recorded as outcome="success", identical to a correct read.
payload_or_id.impact: Clients silently observe outdated data for an unbounded period (evictor.py's bug means it never self-heals via TTL expiry).

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) returns successfully with another key's value
payload_or_id.description: A client's get_value call returns without error but with a value that was written for a different key, because Storage's comma-delimited file format misassigns a line to the wrong key on read. Recorded as outcome="success", identical to a correct read.
payload_or_id.impact: Clients silently receive data belonging to a different key -- a correctness and data-isolation failure with no error signal anywhere.

payload_or_id.title: Process memory grows without bound until the service is unavailable
payload_or_id.description: Cache._entries (cache.py) gains one entry per unique key ever requested and is never trimmed, since evictor.run_eviction_pass never evicts anything. Under sustained unique-key traffic, process memory grows without bound until the process is OOM-killed or degrades until it stops serving get_value calls.

Requires two overlapping put() calls, which the current single periodic-job write path does not exercise -- low likelihood given today's architecture. payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() fails to persist a write
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (storage.py) wraps any OSError raised while reading the existing file, creating parent directories, or writing the replacement file as StorageError. Reachable only via admin.update_value(), the internal write path used by an external periodic data-sync job -- not directly by get_value.
payload_or_id.impact: The intended new value never reaches storage; nothing in this codebase surfaces the failure (admin.update_value has no try/except of its own), so it is only as visible as whatever the external caller does with a raised exception.

payload_or_id.title: admin.update_value writes to storage without invalidating the cache
payload_or_id.description: admin.update_value() (admin.py) calls storage.put(key, value) but never calls Cache.evict(key). Any reader who has already cached that key -- including a cached negative ('not found') result from before the key existed -- keeps observing the pre-write value or absence indefinitely, since nothing else in the read path re-validates a cached entry against storage.
payload_or_id.impact: Establishes the divergence between cache and storage that later manifests to a client as a stale read.

payload_or_id.title: evictor.run_eviction_pass never evicts any entry (seconds vs. milliseconds bug)
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (evictor.py) computes now = time.time() (seconds) and compares now - entry.inserted_at_ms (milliseconds) against TTL_SECONDS. Because inserted_at_ms is ~1000x larger than a seconds-based now, the difference is always a large negative number and the 'expired' condition is never true. No entry is ever evicted, for any key, ever.
payload_or_id.impact: Removes the only safety net that would otherwise bound both cache size and how long a stale entry can persist -- it is the root cause of both unbounded memory growth and permanent (rather than TTL-bounded) staleness.

payload_or_id.title: Storage's flat-file format has no escaping for its comma/newline delimiters
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/put (storage.py) persist one 'key,value' pair per line using an unescaped comma and split records on newlines via splitlines(). A key containing a comma is truncated to the text before its first comma on read (str.partition(',')), so it can silently match a different, shorter key's line. A value containing a newline is re-split into extra spurious lines on the next read, corrupting how subsequent lines in the file are parsed.
payload_or_id.impact: Root cause of a client silently receiving another key's value, or of downstream file entries becoming unparseable, with no exception raised anywhere.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no locking
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (storage.py) reads the whole file into an `existing` dict, updates one key, then rewrites the whole file. Two put() calls whose read/write windows interleave each build `existing` from a stale snapshot; whichever writes last overwrites the other's change with no error raised to either caller.
payload_or_id.impact: A legitimate write can be silently dropped under concurrent writers, with the same client-visible effect as a stale read for the lost key. Requires more than one concurrent writer of the internal write path to manifest.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get/put only catch OSError, not the full space of I/O-adjacent exceptions
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/put (storage.py) call Path.read_text()/write_text() with no explicit encoding, using the platform's default text codec, and catch only 'except OSError'. A value containing characters not encodable in that codec raises UnicodeEncodeError from put(); a file containing bytes not decodable in that codec (including as a side effect of fm-storage-flatfile-delimiter-ambiguity corrupting the file) raises UnicodeDecodeError from get(). Neither is an OSError, so neither is wrapped as StorageError.
payload_or_id.impact: The exception reaches api.get_value() as a type its 'except StorageError' clause does not match, so it is not merely undetected by the outcome metric -- it skips that except block entirely and the metric is not incremented at all, breaking get_value's implicit contract that failures surface as StorageError.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) returns successfully with a stale value
payload_or_id.description: A client's get_value call returns without error but with a value (or a cached 'not found') that no longer matches current storage, because Cache.get() serves whatever it captured on first read/miss with nothing in the read path re-validating it. payload_or_id.impact: Clients silently observe outdated data for an unbounded period (evictor.py's bug means it never self-heals via TTL expiry).

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get() fails to read the backing flat file
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get() (storage.py) wraps any OSError raised while reading the backing file (permission denied, disk I/O error, path unreadable) as StorageError. Occurs on every get_value call that misses the cache while the file is in this state.
payload_or_id.impact: Every cache-missing get_value call for any key fails until the underlying condition (permissions, disk) is fixed.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) raises StorageError to its caller
payload_or_id.description: api.get_value() (api.py) catches StorageError only to record GET_VALUE_REQUESTS{outcome="error"} before re-raising it unchanged. A client's call throws instead of returning a value.
payload_or_id.impact: The sole client-facing operation fails outright for the affected key(s) until the underlying storage condition clears.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.put() fails to persist a write
payload_or_id.description: Storage.put() (storage.py) wraps any OSError raised while reading the existing file, creating parent directories, or writing the replacement file as StorageError. Reachable only via admin.update_value(), the internal write path used by an external periodic data-sync job -- not directly by get_value.
payload_or_id.impact: The intended new value never reaches storage; nothing in this codebase surfaces the failure (admin.update_value has no try/except of its own), so it is only as visible as whatever the external caller does with a raised exception.

payload_or_id.title: evictor.run_eviction_pass never evicts any entry (seconds vs. milliseconds bug)
payload_or_id.description: run_eviction_pass() (evictor.py) computes now = time.time() (seconds) and compares now - entry.inserted_at_ms (milliseconds) against TTL_SECONDS. Because inserted_at_ms is ~1000x larger than a seconds-based now, the difference is always a large negative number and the 'expired' condition is never true. No entry is ever evicted, for any key, ever.
payload_or_id.impact: Removes the only safety net that would otherwise bound both cache size and how long a stale entry can persist -- it is the root cause of both unbounded memory growth and permanent (rather than TTL-bounded) staleness.

payload_or_id.title: Process memory grows without bound until the service is unavailable
payload_or_id.description: Cache._entries (cache.py) gains one entry per unique key ever requested and is never trimmed, since evictor.run_eviction_pass never evicts anything. Under sustained unique-key traffic, process memory grows without bound until the process is OOM-killed or degrades until it stops serving get_value calls.
payload_or_id.impact: Total service outage: every client's get_value call fails, not just calls for affected keys.

payload_or_id.title: Storage.get/put only catch OSError, not the full space of I/O-adjacent exceptions
payload_or_id.description: Storage.get/put (storage.py) call Path.read_text()/write_text() with no explicit encoding, using the platform's default text codec, and catch only 'except OSError'. A value containing characters not encodable in that codec raises UnicodeEncodeError from put(); a file containing bytes not decodable in that codec (including as a side effect of fm-storage-flatfile-delimiter-ambiguity corrupting the file) raises UnicodeDecodeError from get(). Neither is an OSError, so neither is wrapped as StorageError.
payload_or_id.impact: The exception reaches api.get_value() as a type its 'except StorageError' clause does not match, so it is not merely undetected by the outcome metric -- it skips that except block entirely and the metric is not incremented at all, breaking get_value's implicit contract that failures surface as StorageError.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) raises an exception that isn't StorageError
payload_or_id.description: A client's get_value call raises an exception whose type is neither StorageError nor documented anywhere in api.py, because api.get_value()'s except clause only matches StorageError. GET_VALUE_REQUESTS is not incremented for either outcome label in this path.
payload_or_id.impact: Worse than fm-get-value-raises-storage-error: the client still sees a hard failure, but it carries zero metric footprint at all -- not even the existing error counter fires -- and violates the API's only documented failure contract.

payload_or_id.title: get_value(key) returns successfully with a stale value
payload_or_id.description: A client's get_value call returns without error but with a value (or a cached 'not found') that no longer matches current storage, because Cache.get() serves whatever it captured on first read/miss with nothing in the read path re-validating it. Recorded as outcome="success", identical to a correct read.
payload_or_id.impact: Clients silently observe outdated data for an unbounded period (evictor.py's bug means it never self-heals via TTL expiry).
